memo.verdict: PARK to the active watchlist. Direction neutral on the business, unfavourable on the near-term entry. Conviction medium. Grade [C]. The memo does not progress MRK-DE to Early-Stage Assessment. Its one-line statement of the decision: a good business at a full price, on incomplete evidence, with sell-side earnings momentum in the bottom quartile. Four park reasons, in the memo's order. One, the valuation questions failed inside the framework: Element E1 Required Attribute RA2 asks about mispricing and about a low trading multiple, and both grade [D], so the change-from-current is thin at EUR 136.30. Two, case simplicity: four of five guardrails fail, making the case expensive to underwrite and to monitor for the return now on offer. Three, the evidence base: three of six research families describe Merck & Co, so Viewforth holds no valid risk research on Merck KGaA. Four, earnings momentum: sell-side earnings estimates were cut nineteen times over twelve months and the composite momentum reading is minus 14.
case: The case for the business, and why it nearly justified another stage.

Change forces are the strongest part of the case and grade [B] on both legs at once, which the memo calls rarer than it sounds in large-cap pharmaceuticals. The external leg has two components. Bioprocessing consumables have turned: Process Solutions grew 16.2% organically in Q1 2026, passed EUR 1bn of quarterly sales and beat consensus by 5%, with Deutsche Bank resting its plausibility verdict on book-to-bill ratios comfortably above 1.00. Company guidance targets around 10% bioprocessing consumables expansion and consensus models 10.20%. The sector confirms it is real rather than company-specific: Sartorius reported 7.50% group constant-currency growth and Lonza reiterated 11.00% to 12.00% organic guidance. Semiconductor materials is the second component, guided at a 7% to 11% mid-term organic rate against consensus of 8.30%, with Semiconductor Solutions growing 7.50% organically in Q1 2026 on low-double-digit growth in advanced materials. The mechanism is materials intensity rising 200 to 400 basis points as customers migrate to sub-seven-nanometre nodes, which lets Merck outgrow underlying wafer volumes. Ground-level confirmation came from the Head of Metrology and Inspection Applications at Merck Electronics, who confirmed booming process-control demand for artificial-intelligence device packaging at TSMC and record-high Thin Films sales.

The internal leg is a chief executive, a strategy, a structure and a capital cycle changing together inside eighteen months. Kai Beckmann became chief executive on 1 May 2026, succeeding Belen Garijo after a structured multi-month transition; he has 37 years with the group and has served on the Executive Board since 2011. He unveiled the "Velocity" playbook covering integrated workflow solutions, group-wide artificial-intelligence capability and speed to market. Life Science moved to a customer-centric model from 1 January 2026 in three units, Process Solutions, Advanced Solutions and Discovery Solutions, which Jefferies reads as improving capital discipline and margin durability. Free cash flow formally replaced operating cash flow as the primary group performance measure from fiscal 2026. More than EUR 7bn was deployed across 30 manufacturing sites since 2021 and capital spending is now transitioning to maintenance-weighted, with Q1 2026 operating cash flow up 47.2% to EUR 818m and free cash flow at EUR 291m against EUR 1m. The USD 11.3bn Bio-Techne acquisition announced on 25 June 2026 targets technology leadership in next-generation multi-omics and proteomics.
counter_case: The counter-case is what carried the decision, and the memo treats it as decisive rather than as balance.

The entry price has closed, and the framework says so inside Element E1 Required Attribute RA2 rather than deferring it. Two of that attribute's five questions grade [D]. On mispricing: shares have risen 26.0% from the EUR 108.20 trough of 29 April 2026 to EUR 136.30, so the re-rating is behind, not ahead; EUR 136.30 sits above Morgan Stanley's EUR 135, Jefferies' EUR 129, Deutsche Bank's EUR 125 and Bernstein's EUR 121, with Redburn's EUR 179 the sole bull target and the consensus mean of EUR 141.47 implying only 3.80% upside; the 15% conglomerate discount Bernstein applies has persisted for years and is not a fresh mispricing to arbitrage. On the multiple: the dashboard 14.5x is stale, since 14.5x on EUR 8.87 forward earnings implies a price near EUR 128.6, while EUR 136.30 divided by EUR 8.87 gives approximately 15.4x, above the 15.0x industry average; Deutsche Bank calls 15x 2027 earnings "not cheap, fair" and Jefferies judges the structural growth drivers already fairly rewarded. The memo also applies a grading discipline here: a 34th own-history percentile is an own-history level, not a cross-sectional cheapness rank.
triggers: Re-activation triggers, any one of which returns the case to the desk. Price below EUR 121, the lowest named broker target, restoring roughly the headroom the April trough offered. Corrected Merck KGaA business-foundations and risks families on disk, identity-confirmed by content. Two consecutive quarters of Process Solutions organic growth inside the guided 8% to 12% band with book-to-bill above 1.00. A positive one-month and three-month sell-side earnings revision count, showing the [F] momentum grade has genuinely turned.

Kill criteria. Process Solutions book-to-bill below 1.00 or quarterly growth below 8%, which would recast the Q1 surge as Asian safety-stock building rather than recovery. Group EBITDA margin breaking the 28% baseline under the stacked downside of an academic funding freeze, fast Mavenclad erosion and dollar weakness. Evidence that bioprocessing share donation is continuing, which would turn the central growth engine from a recovery story into a structural decline story.

Monitoring thresholds carried forward. Process Solutions book-to-bill expected above 1.00, warning below 1.00, reviewed quarterly. Process Solutions quarterly growth expected between 8% and 12%, warning below 8%. Semiconductor materials growth expected at 7% to 11%, warning below 5%. Currency headwind on sales guided at minus 4% to minus 1%, warning worse than minus 4%. US Mavenclad erosion from May 2026, warning on a faster-than-guided margin drop.
What would move the view bullish. A retest below EUR 121 with two clean quarters of Process Solutions growth in band and a positive three-month revision count.
What would move the view bearish. An Electronics margin that falls materially once one-off gains are stripped out, confirming the false-friend reading at Element E8 Required Attribute RA8.

Open questions the memo could not answer on the evidence available. No correct-issuer source quantifies oil-price or energy-cost sensitivity, so Element E5 Required Attribute RA3 is graded qualitatively. No correct-issuer source addresses whether new contract pricing has stabilised, so Element E8 Required Attribute RA6 Core Question 4 is tagged factual and left unevidenced. No correct-issuer source addresses single-use versus stainless-steel substitution or chromatography resin alternatives, limiting Element E11 Required Attribute RA2 Core Question 5. No tariff impact is quantified for Merck KGaA, and the only tariff datapoint in the sources belongs to Sartorius and was deliberately not carried across. No peer in the named set carries a ratings file and three carry no digest, so every peer-relative grade rests on digest commentary and sector characteristics.
